test_title: SSC CGL 2022 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On : 03 Dec 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

I __am been working here__ for the past ten years.
solution:
The correct answer is: **have been working here**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• '**Been**' is used to indicate an action that took part in the past or an earlier time.
 
• As the past participle, '**been**' in the form of '**be**' is used in the present perfect and past perfect tense.
 
• In this sentence, it is said that the speaker has been working here for ten years.
 
• Therefore, "**the present perfect continuous tense**" should be used here.
 
• The structure follows: **Subject + have/has + been + verb (ing) + the rest of the sentence__**
 
• Therefore, only option 1 is following the exact rule.
 
• Thus, **option 1** is the correct answer.

 

**Corrected sentence: ***__I have been working here for the past ten years. __*
